title: Sell Mineral Rights in Tiltonsville, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tiltonsville, OH | Old Deeds
metaDescription: Tiltonsville, Jefferson County mineral owner with an old, faded, or hard-to-read deed? Learn how to confirm ownership and sell your Utica flank interest.
heroLead: River and rail towns like Tiltonsville tend to have some of the oldest recorded deeds in eastern Ohio, and old paper means old handwriting, faded ink, and legal descriptions that read nothing like a modern deed.
intro: Tiltonsville sits along the Ohio River in Jefferson County, on the flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play. The town's history as a river and rail stop goes back well over a century, and mineral rights reservations tied to the surrounding hillside farms are often recorded in deeds from the late 1800s or early 1900s.
If you have a copy of an old severance deed for land near Tiltonsville and cannot quite make sense of it, that is common, and it does not prevent you from confirming and selling your interest.

sections.heading: Reading a century-old mineral reservation
paragraphs: Older deeds often use metes-and-bounds legal descriptions, referencing landmarks, adjoining owners' names, or surveyor's chains rather than the section-township-range system used more consistently today. They may also use archaic language for the type of interest reserved.
None of that makes the deed invalid. It just takes someone familiar with older Jefferson County land records to translate it into current terms, which is part of the title work we do before quoting.

sections.heading: Tracing ownership from a deed that old to you
paragraphs: Between an 1890s reservation and today, land near Tiltonsville has likely passed through several generations via wills, probate, and possibly additional deeds. Each of those transfers needs to be documented to establish your current percentage.
The Jefferson County Recorder's office in Steubenville holds this chain, and we search it directly so you are not stuck deciphering old paperwork yourself.

sections.heading: What your confirmed interest is worth
paragraphs: Once ownership is established, we check current activity for the specific township around Tiltonsville and put together a written offer based on documented lease status and nearby production, not a general assumption about the area.
Old paper does not mean an outdated or lesser interest; it simply requires more careful tracing to confirm.

faqs.question: My deed near Tiltonsville is from the 1890s and hard to read. Is it still valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, age alone does not invalidate a deed. We regularly work with 19th-century reservations as part of standard title research.

faqs.question: The legal description in my old deed does not look like a normal address. What is that?
faqs.answer: That is likely a metes-and-bounds description, a common older format using landmarks and directions instead of a modern lot or section number. We translate it as part of the title search.

faqs.question: How many generations of ownership do you need to trace?
faqs.answer: As many as it takes to reach you from the original reservation. We handle that research directly using county recorder records.
